blocks.headline: Hobbys
blocks.bodyEnglish:
These ten hobbies are the core words of Lektion 2.
Say each word with its meaning.

blocks.headline: Was machst du gern?
blocks.bodyEnglish: Two classmates ask each other about hobbies. Notice the three different answers: yes a lot, not really, so-so.

turns.speaker: A
turns.english: Do you like listening to music?

turns.speaker: A
turns.english: Do you like going to the cinema?

blocks.title: Drei Antworten auf »… gern?«
blocks.bodyEnglish:
There are three standard answers.
»Ja, sehr gern.« = yes, a lot.
»Nein, nicht so gern.« = not really.
»Es geht so.« = so-so.
blocks.bodyGerman:
Ja, sehr gern.
Nein, nicht so gern.
Es geht so.

blocks.headline: Das Verb bei »ich« und »du«
blocks.bodyEnglish:
Every German verb changes its ending with the person.
A few verbs also change the vowel: lesen → du liest.

blocks.explanationEnglish:
German has one present tense. It covers now, today and every day.
Take the infinitive, drop -en and add the ending for the person.
Full set: ich -e, du -st, er/sie/es -t, wir -en, ihr -t, sie/Sie -en.
Some verbs change the vowel: lesen → du liest, singen → du singst.
Trap: Sie takes -en like they. ✗ Sie kocht. → ✓ Sie kochen.
blocks.englishBridge: English keeps one form: I cook, you cook, we cook. German marks every person: ich koche, du kochst, er kocht.

blocks.title: Hobbys mit gern
blocks.explanationEnglish: gern means 'like to'. It comes directly after the conjugated verb. To ask, put the verb first: Kochst du gern?

blocks.title: »Du koche«
blocks.bodyEnglish:
The du-form takes -st, not -e.
✗ Du koche gern. → ✓ Du kochst gern.
Some verbs also change the vowel.
✗ Du lese. → ✓ Du liest.
blocks.bodyGerman:
Du kochst gern.
Du liest gern.

blocks.explanationEnglish:
nicht means not. It makes a sentence or a phrase negative.
Put nicht after the conjugated verb: Ich koche nicht.
With an object, nicht goes before the object or to the end.
For a soft hobby answer use nicht so gern.
Trap: ✗ Ich nicht koche gern. → ✓ Ich koche nicht gern.
blocks.englishBridge: English needs do for a question and puts not after it: I do not cook. German puts nicht at the end.
blocks.targetSentenceEnglish: I do not like to cook.

examples.english: I do not work on Sunday.

items.english: What do you like to do?
Do you like listening to music?
Do you like going to the cinema?

blocks.explanationEnglish: du takes -st: spielen → du spielst. 'spiele' is the ich-form, 'spielt' is er/sie or ihr.
